workingTitle: Water as the medium for life

officialGuide.requirementSummary: First cells originated in water; water remains the medium for most life processes.

workingTitle: Polar covalent bonds and hydrogen bonding

officialGuide.requirementSummary: Polar covalent bonding arises from unequal electron sharing; show hydrogen bonds between polar water molecules.
Hydrogen-bonded cohesion permits tension in xylem and makes surface tension a habitat feature.
Adhesion to polar or charged materials causes capillary movement in soil and plant cell walls.
Water dissolves many hydrophilic substances for metabolism and transport; hydrophobic molecules have essential roles.

workingTitle: Physical properties of water and aquatic habitats

officialGuide.requirementSummary: Compare buoyancy, viscosity, thermal conductivity and specific heat of air and water and their effects on aquatic animals.

workingTitle: The origin and retention of Earth’s water

officialGuide.requirementSummary: Consider the asteroid-delivery hypothesis; gravity and low enough temperature for condensation explain retention.

workingTitle: Water and the search for extraterrestrial life

officialGuide.requirementSummary: Connect searching for extraterrestrial life with water and the Goldilocks zone.
